paragraphs.text: A self-watering pot makes it easier to care for houseplants, especially for people who are often away. It consists of two parts: an inner pot that holds the soil and the plant, and an outer container that holds water.
Between the two parts is a water reservoir. A thin rope made of cotton, called a wick, runs from the soil down into the water and draws moisture up to the roots as the soil dries out.
A narrow tube at the side allows the owner to refill the reservoir without lifting the plant. A small float inside the tube rises and falls to show how much water is left.
Depending on the size of the plant, a full reservoir can last for two to three weeks. Owners should still check the soil from time to time, as plants need less water in winter.
Self-watering pots are sold in many sizes, from small ones for windowsills to large pots for balconies.
